Route by size
Small text edits to kilo (free) or a cheaper claude model, bigger changes to claude. The runner can pick from the note length, or you pick.

Done: 🧭 auto routing (notes up to 500 chars and no structural words → kilo free; up to 2,000 → claude haiku; larger or structural → claude). Picking an agent by hand always overrides. Evals cover the rules.
Auto-deploy on push
A GitHub Action runs fly deploy on every push to main. Fits trunk-based development and removes the laptop from the deploy step. Needs a Fly token as a GitHub secret; keep it short-lived.

Written, not yet working: .github/workflows/deploy.yml deploys on every push to main. It needs YOUR one-time step: fly tokens create deploy -a day-2-short --expiry 168h, then gh secret set FLY_API_TOKEN. Until then the runner and deploy_and_wait.py still deploy. A 7-day token expires, so renew it.
Stop committing site/ and the 22 root redirect pages
Build site/ inside the Docker image. Diffs and patches get much smaller. Keep only the tiny GitHub Pages redirect.

Done: site/, MASTER_SPEC.md and deployed.json are untracked; the Dockerfile builds site/ in a Python stage (tested with docker build and on Fly). Only index.html (the GitHub Pages redirect) stays tracked. Trade-off: old deep links on the GitHub address (for example /day-2/s2-w.html) no longer redirect; only the root does.
tech: Not a token saver for the spec or the log: those are text the agent edits and git is the audit trail. It does help your review ticks and notes, which live in each browser's localStorage and reset on a new device or address. A small SQLite database on a Fly volume (about 1 GB, cheap) keeps them across devices and lets the agent ask for only the unresolved feedback (a few hundred tokens instead of a pasted dump). Cost: a small server and a volume instead of static nginx. Do it after items 1–4.

Not worth it: 23 mostly static pages, 0.08 s build. React adds a build chain and more code for the agent to read. If you want components, Astro (Markdown plus small interactive parts) fits better, but only if the Python generator becomes painful after splitting it. The notes panel and the sandbox can stay plain JavaScript.

producer_intro: From general short-form practice, not from your analytics yet. Treat each as a test: change one thing per upload and compare the numbers on S2-08 and the Day 1 analytics page.
producer: Hook
Show the payoff in the first frame

Put 'King − Man + Woman = Queen' on screen at second 0, big, with the voice already speaking. No logo, no 'hi', no intro. The viewer should know the promise in under a second, and the first clip (c1) should already move.
Hook
Open a question, close it at the end
The title and first line ask 'how does AI know this?' The answer lands only in the last clip. Keep the one open loop; do not answer early.
Retention
Make the end flow into the start
Rewatches count. The last word should lead into the first word and the last frame should match the first (your S2-06 loop checks). The tiny 9246 in the Queen rewards a second watch.
Retention
Change something every 2 to 3 seconds
A cut, a zoom, a caption change or a new object. Your 6 clips of about 6 to 9 seconds each need a visible change inside each clip. Fix c1 (8.8 s) and c3 (9.3 s), which are longer than one Flow clip.
Retention
Cut every second that does not teach
After the first assembly, remove pauses and filler; the cut should end the instant the point lands. Watch it once muted and once with sound, and note the exact second where your attention drops.
Quality
Voice first, then picture
A clear voice with even pacing carries a Short. Keep the ElevenLabs take clean (no clipping), leave a short breath before the key line, and keep music far below the voice.
Quality
Check loudness and the phone speaker
Listen on a phone at normal volume. YouTube normalises around −14 LUFS; aim near that and avoid peaks that clip.
Quality
Render all text in Remotion, never in Flow
AI-generated text inside clips is often garbled. Equations, captions and the number 9246 should be drawn by Remotion so they are sharp and correct, in the safe area, large.
Quality
One style bible for all six clips
Reuse the same style sentence and camera preset in every prompt, keep the palette and lighting consistent, and re-generate a clip that looks like a different video. Consistency reads as quality.
Packaging
Title and thumbnail are part of the hook
Lead the title with the equation and one curiosity word, and keep it short enough not to be cut on a phone. The first frame is the thumbnail on many surfaces, so make frame 0 readable.
Packaging
Pin a question that is easy to answer
Pinned comment: one line the viewer can answer in a word (for example: 'Which word would you try: pride or vanity?'). Replies raise engagement and give you next-video ideas.
Value
Give one takeaway and one thing to try
One sentence a viewer can repeat: 'meaning becomes coordinates, and nearby points mean similar things.' In the description link the sandbox page so people can try pride − vanity + honor themselves.
Value
Be honest about the simplification
One line in the description or pinned comment: real models are fuzzier than the clean equation. That builds trust and protects you from the first 'actually…' comment.
Measure
Decide the next hook from the numbers

After 24 hours and 7 days record views, average view duration, the share who swiped away early and rewatches on S2-08. Compare with Day 1. Change only one thing (hook line, first frame or pace) for Day 3.
Series
Make the series the reason to come back
End on a one-line teaser for the next day (Day 3: attention) and keep the same intro look, voice and caption style, so viewers recognise it in a feed.
Process
Run one pre-flight pass before every upload

Frame 0 readable, first 2 seconds move, no clip longer than one beat, text correct, loop checked, loudness checked on a phone, title and pinned comment ready, sources and the honest line in the description.
